request.query:
SPSS will not start on Mac


I downloaded SPSS about 3 weeks ago. On the day when I downloaded it, it was working fine. Last week, I tried starting SPSS but it did not start. I tried reinstalling it, it still would not open. I've updated JAVA (thought this would be a problem), it slowly opened the program but then now that I have reinstalled it and entered in my code, I've used up my code and I have no authorization. But just now, I started SPSS and the same problem is happening. The IBM SPSS name screen appears but nothing happens.

    SPSS would not start.

    Even if it does start, I have licensing problems.

payload.answer:
IBM SPSS Statistics (any version) has two issues to resolve before it will run on OS X 10.10: 

1. Download and re-install Apple Java 6

- After the OS upgrade is finished, Apple Java 6 no longer exists on their system. 
- The first time the user runs an application that relies on Java 6, the OS pops up a dialog box stating they've requested Java 6, but none is present.
- The Java dialog has a "More Info" button, which when clicked opens a browser to an Apple Tech Support page for Apple Java 2014-001. A download link is provided (http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572 [http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572]).
- User must click on the download link and a DMG containing the Java 6 installer is downloaded.
- User must open the Java DMG, then double click on the Java installer, follow the prompts and complete the installation.

2. Re-license Statistics

- We use Safenet Sentinel technology for licensing. Safenet writes hidden data somewhere on-disc for keeping track of licensing data.
- The OS X 10.10 upgrade process erases that hidden data. Attempting to run Statistics produces a licensing error and Stats does not start/run properly.
- Solution: Re-run the SPSS License Authorization Wizard, enter auth code again and complete licensing procedure.
- Statistics will now run normally. [S5]

A. A temporary issue with communication between the trial product and IBM.com was blocking the authentication required to start the software. This issue has been resolved and you should now be able to start your software correctly. 

Q. Why can't I use my authorization code on downloaded trial? 
A. IBM SPSS Statistics Trial software has been updated to a new licensing model. Rather than using an authorization code to obtain a license for your product, your IBM ID is used in its place. If you require access to an install which requires an authorization code to license your product, please contact IBM SPSS Technical Support. Your support options can be found on the Predictive Analytics Community Help Page: https://developer.ibm.com/predictiveanalytics/get-help/ [https://developer.ibm.com/predictiveanalytics/get-help/]

Q: What is the length of the trial download for IBM SPSS Statistics Software? 
A: 14 days for IBM SPSS Statistics. 

Q: Will the Trial subscription auto-renewal be cancelled automatically? 
A: Yes. When the Trial time period has lapsed the subscription will be automatically cancelled. No further action on your part is required to cancel your subscription.

IBM SPSS Statistics (any version) has two issues to resolve before it will run on OS X 10.10: 

1. Download and re-install Apple Java 6

- After the OS upgrade is finished, Apple Java 6 no longer exists on their system. 
- The first time the user runs an application that relies on Java 6, the OS pops up a dialog box stating they've requested Java 6, but none is present.
- The Java dialog has a "More Info" button, which when clicked opens a browser to an Apple Tech Support page for Apple Java 2014-001. A download link is provided (http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572 [http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572]).
- User must click on the download link and a DMG containing the Java 6 installer is downloaded.
- User must open the Java DMG, then double click on the Java installer, follow the prompts and complete the installation.

2. Re-license Statistics

- We use Safenet Sentinel technology for licensing. Safenet writes hidden data somewhere on-disc for keeping track of licensing data.
- The OS X 10.10 upgrade process erases that hidden data. Attempting to run Statistics produces a licensing error and Stats does not start/run properly.
- Solution: Re-run the SPSS License Authorization Wizard, enter auth code again and complete licensing procedure.
- Statistics will now run normally.

IBM SPSS Statistics (any version) has two issues to resolve before it will run on OS X 10.10: 

1. Download and re-install Apple Java 6

- After the OS upgrade is finished, Apple Java 6 no longer exists on their system. 
- The first time the user runs an application that relies on Java 6, the OS pops up a dialog box stating they've requested Java 6, but none is present.
- The Java dialog has a "More Info" button, which when clicked opens a browser to an Apple Tech Support page for Apple Java 2014-001. A download link is provided (http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572 [http://support.apple.com/kb/dl1572]).
- User must click on the download link and a DMG containing the Java 6 installer is downloaded.
- User must open the Java DMG, then double click on the Java installer, follow the prompts and complete the installation.

2. Re-license Statistics

- We use Safenet Sentinel technology for licensing. Safenet writes hidden data somewhere on-disc for keeping track of licensing data.
- The OS X 10.10 upgrade process erases that hidden data. Attempting to run Statistics produces a licensing error and Stats does not start/run properly.
- Solution: Re-run the SPSS License Authorization Wizard, enter auth code again and complete licensing procedure.
- Statistics will now run normally.
